  The bounded-distinct-prime and finite-prime-support REG-immunity
  corollaries are the main language-theoretic consequences; bounded
  almost-prime and prime-language REG-immunity are weaker downstream
  cases. The slice-rigidity statement
  \(\Cref{prop:zeckendorf-regular-slice-rigidity}\) remains a separate
  density-scale obstruction, while the nonregularity corollary
  \(\Cref{cor:zeckendorf-prime-language-not-regular}\) follows
  immediately from REG-immunity. The sofic-slice exclusion
  \(\Cref{rem:zeckendorf-primes-not-sofic}\) is then a short consequence
  of regularity of sofic block languages.

  \item \textbf{Context-free, MCFL, and Pisot extensions.}
  Fixed-base prime CF-immunity is classical. Hartmanis and Shank proved
  that no infinite set of primes can be accepted in fixed-base notation
  by a pushdown automaton; Sch\"utzenberger obtained the conclusion
  independently \cite{HartmanisShank1968,Schutzenberger1968}. We do not
  reproduce their proofs as new. Our use of Ogden's lemma
  \cite{Ogden1968} instead couples the two pumped blocks to the
  Zeckendorf unimodular action and yields the stronger coprime-quotient
  chain
  \Cref{thm:context-free-coprime-quotient-zeckendorf-pumping}. The
  weak pumping lemma of Seki--Matsumura--Fujii--Kasami
  \cite{SekiEtAl1991} supplies one synchronized \(2k\)-block orbit for
  every infinite \(k\)-MCFL; it is used as an input, not reproved.
  Kanazawa--Kobele--Michaelis--Salvati--Yoshinaka prove that the usual
  strong pumping form fails in general
  \cite{KanazawaKobeleMichaelisSalvatiYoshinaka2014}, and the recent
  substitution lemma of Duncan--Elder--Frenkel--Liu gives a different
  strong interface \cite{DuncanElderFrenkelLiu2026}. Neither result
  concerns recurrence numeration or divisibility. The new deductions
  are the fixed local-congruence orbit
  \Cref{thm:mcfl-synchronized-congruence-orbit}, the topological
  fingerprint \Cref{thm:mcfl-local-adic-fingerprint}, the exact rank
  formula \Cref{prop:local-prime-factor-cb-rank}, and the escape
  dichotomy \Cref{thm:nonunit-mcfl-escape-dichotomy}. The unit-system
  constructions are \Cref{thm:unit-mcfl-deep-congruence-chain} and
  \Cref{thm:unit-mcfl-divisibility-tree}.
  Evertse's theorem on prime ideals in ratios of terms of
  nondegenerate recurrences \cite{Evertse1984} is used as an arithmetic
  input to the geometric-ray characterization
  \Cref{thm:bounded-outside-support-geometric-ray}; it is not claimed as
  a new recurrence theorem.
  Broughan's \(\mathbb Q\)- and Cantor-space classifications for adic
  integer topologies are cited as classical inputs
  \cite{Broughan2003}. Frougny normalization and the
  Bertrand/substitution literature
  \cite{Frougny1992,BruyereHansel1997,Fabre1995,FrougnySolomyak1992}
  supply the canonical finite-state numeration interface, not the
  arithmetic pumping proof. The residual nonunit and non-positional
  limits are stated in \Cref{rem:pisot-open-interfaces}. The
  recurrence-witness separation
  \Cref{prop:recurrence-witness-separation} distinguishes the invariant
  minimal action from an arbitrarily inflated companion presentation.

  \item \textbf{Analytic obstructions: classical background.}
  \suppref{Theorem~A.1} is the usual
  P\'olya--Carlson natural-boundary mechanism for Euler products.
  \suppref{Proposition~A.2} is the corresponding
  periodicity obstruction for determinant models after \(z=e^{-s}\). Both are
  classical
  \cite{Polya1923,Carlson1921,Estermann1928,ArtinMazur1965,BowenLanford1970}.
\end{itemize}
\smallskip
\noindent\textbf{Relation to density and approximation literature.} For ordinary
automatic sets, asymptotic density questions go back at least to
Berstel \cite{Berstel1973}; the standard global sources include
B\"uchi's automata-theoretic decidability work \cite{Buchi1960} and
Allouche--Shallit's monograph on automatic sequences
\cite{AlloucheShallit2003}. Matrix and algorithmic treatments appear
in
\cite{BodirskyGaertnerVonOertzenSchwinghammer2004,Bell2020UpperDensity},
and Koga's paper \cite{Koga2019Density} revisits Sin'ya's density-zero
criterion \cite{Sinya2021}. The rational-measure viewpoint of Hansel
and Perrin \cite{HanselPerrin1989} interprets regular languages via
probability measures on shifts of finite type. Kozik's MFCS 2005 paper
\cite{Kozik2005Conditional} formulates conditional densities for
deterministic presentations in the trim strongly connected setting,
Montoya \cite{Montoya2025Relative} recasts these questions in terms of
relative densities, and Berth\'e--Goulet-Ouellet--Perrin
\cite{BertheGouletPerrin2025} establish a broad density theorem under
shift-invariant measures. Accordingly,
\suppref{Theorem~1.2}, \Cref{prop:zeckendorf-regular-powerlaw}, and
\suppref{Theorem~1.18}
should be read here as background statements in a form suited to the
prime-slice applications, while
\suppref{Theorem~1.14} is the exponent-sensitive
extension needed for general trim deterministic presentations. Cobham's
theorem
\cite{Cobham1969} is the foundational reference for base-dependent
automatic recognizability of sets of integers. Regular approximation of
non-regular languages is a separate line of work; see, for example,
Eisman and Ravikumar \cite{EismanRavikumar2005} and the asymptotic
approximation framework of Sin'ya \cite{Sinya2021}. Polynomial and
sparse growth phenomena for regular languages are part of the classical
transfer-matrix picture \cite{Berstel1973,SalomaaSoittola1978}, and
numeration systems on regular languages are treated in
\cite{LecomteRigo2001,Frougny1992,BruyereHansel1997,CharlierRampersad2011,Rigo2014Vol1,Rigo2014Vol2}.
The present contribution is narrower: it packages the fixed-DFA
prime-slice obstruction with computable residue-class constants and
explicit thresholds, then applies the same finite-budget argument in the
Zeckendorf setting.


\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Summary.} \suppref{Theorem~1.2 and Lemma~1.16} and
\Cref{prop:zeckendorf-regular-powerlaw}
record the density statements needed for deterministic presentations.
\suppref{Theorem~1.14} gives the general trim
deterministic finite-budget theorem, including multiple maximal
components, Perron-active residue classes, and their polynomial factors,
and \suppref{Theorem~1.18} records the strongly connected
specialization used for Zeckendorf. The paper's effective contribution
is the finite-budget obstruction mechanism with quantitative fixed-DFA
recall/precision and symmetric-difference instances; see
\suppref{Corollary~1.19}, \suppref{Proposition~1.9},
\suppref{Corollary~1.10}, and \suppref{Corollary~1.12}.
The Zeckendorf analogues are
\Cref{cor:zeck-symmetric-diff,cor:zeck-recall-precision}. The
Zeckendorf prime-language theorem is downstream of the PNT-free
coprime-quotient pumping theorem
\Cref{thm:coprime-quotient-zeckendorf-pumping}. Its principal
consequences are
\Cref{cor:unbounded-distinct-prime-divisors,cor:bounded-distinct-prime-zeckendorf-languages-reg-immune}
and \Cref{cor:finite-prime-support-zeckendorf-languages-reg-immune};
\Cref{prop:zeckendorf-regular-slice-rigidity} remains a separate
slice-cardinality obstruction, and
\Cref{cor:zeckendorf-prime-language-not-regular} is an immediate
consequence of REG-immunity.
Context-free Zeckendorf pumping is
\Cref{thm:context-free-coprime-quotient-zeckendorf-pumping}, with the
immunity consequences in
\Cref{cor:zeckendorf-context-free-immunity-package}. The stronger MCFL
package is
\Cref{thm:mcfl-synchronized-congruence-orbit,thm:mcfl-local-adic-fingerprint,prop:local-prime-factor-cb-rank,thm:nonunit-mcfl-escape-dichotomy,thm:bounded-outside-support-geometric-ray,cor:bounded-outside-support-semidecidable,thm:unit-mcfl-deep-congruence-chain,thm:unit-mcfl-divisibility-tree};
its linear Pisot specialization is
\Cref{thm:recurrent-numeration-prime-cf-immunity,cor:linear-pisot-prime-cf-immunity}.
The eventual-sofic exclusion is recorded only as the brief consequence
\Cref{rem:zeckendorf-primes-not-sofic}, while
\suppref{Theorem~A.1} and \suppref{Proposition~A.2}
remain classical background.

\medskip
Finite-automata non-recognizability of the base-\(b\) prime language
goes back to Minsky and Papert \cite{MinskyPapert1966}.
Allen \cite{Allen1968}, Hartmanis--Shank
\cite{HartmanisShank1968}, and Sch\"utzenberger
\cite{Schutzenberger1968} proved stronger related results for broader
language classes and acceptable sets. Shallit's survey and monograph
treat automaticity and number theory from the finite-automata viewpoint
\cite{Shallit1996,AlloucheShallit2003}. Recent work of Yuen and Dubbe
studies regularity and quantitative automaticity around the prime set
\cite{Yuen2022,Dubbe2024}, and Shen proves that prime automata in Yao's
finite-automata primeness model do not exist \cite{Shen2022}. Those
results concern
recognizability or growing-state quantitative automaticity. The present
theorems are different: the automaton is fixed, the comparison is made
on each fixed length slice, and the conclusion is a recall/precision
or symmetric-difference obstruction rather than a state lower bound for
a sequence of automata.

The Zeckendorf theorem in \Cref{sec:zeckendorf} should be compared with,
but not identified with, the classical base-representation results of
Sch\"utzenberger. In a fixed base the digit value update is controlled
by multiplication by the base modulo a prime. For LSD-first Zeckendorf
words the corresponding update is instead the unimodular \(3\times3\)
matrix action on
\((\val(\text{prefix}),F_{r+1},F_{r+2})^t\). This invertibility modulo
the square of the current value is what makes the pumping congruence
work and yields quotients \(Q_i\equiv1\pmod {N_i}\). Thus the quotient
is coprime to the previous value, forcing new rational prime divisors;
the prime-language REG-immunity is the \(K=1\) bounded-distinct-prime
subcase.

430-\begin{theorem}[Nonunit escape dichotomy and MCF-immunity]
431:  \label{thm:nonunit-mcfl-escape-dichotomy}
432-  Let \(L\subseteq\mathcal R_U\) be an infinite MCFL. Then either
433-  \[
434-    \sup_{w\in L}\omega_{S^c}(\val_U(w))=\infty,
435-  \]
436-  or there is a prime \(p\mid a_0\) such that
437-  \[
438-    \sup_{w\in L}v_p(\val_U(w))=\infty.
439-  \]
440-  Consequently the following languages are MCF-immune whenever they are
441-  infinite:
442-  \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
443-    \item the prime representation language \(\mathcal P_U\);
444-    \item every language on which \(\Omega(\val_U(w))\) is bounded;
445-    \item every finite-prime-support language on which all
446-    \(v_p(\val_U(w))\), \(p\mid a_0\), are bounded.
447-  \end{enumerate}
448-  In a unit system, every bounded-\(\omega(\val_U(w))\) language is
449-  MCF-immune.
450-\end{theorem}
451-
452-\begin{proof}
453-  If neither alternative held, finiteness of \(S\) would give
454-  \(K\ge0\) and \(E\in\NN_0^S\) such that
455-  \[
456-    \{\val_U(w):w\in L\}\subseteq X_{K,E}.
457-  \]
458-  By \Cref{prop:local-prime-factor-cb-rank}, \(X_{K,E}\) is scattered.
459-  This contradicts
460-  \Cref{thm:mcfl-local-adic-fingerprint}. Prime values satisfy
461:  \(\omega_{S^c}\le1\) and \(v_p\le1\); bounded \(\Omega\) bounds both
462-  alternatives; and finite prime support bounds \(\omega_{S^c}\), with
463-  the remaining valuations bounded by hypothesis. If \(S=\varnothing\),
464-  the second alternative is absent, giving the unit-system assertion.
465-\end{proof}

470-fixed, while \(v_p(b^n)\) is unbounded for every \(p\mid b\).

803-\begin{theorem}[Prime immunity for recurrent numeration systems]
804-  \label{thm:recurrent-numeration-prime-cf-immunity}
805-  Let \((U,A,\mathcal R_U)\) satisfy \textup{(U1)--(U4)}, and put
806-  \[
807-    \mathcal P_U
808-      :=\{w\in\mathcal R_U:\val_U(w)\text{ is prime}\}.
809-  \]
810-  Then \(\mathcal P_U\) is MCF-immune, and therefore CF-immune,
811-  REG-immune, and not recognizable by a finite automaton over \(A\).
812-
813-  If, in addition, \(\abs{a_0}=1\), then every infinite multiple
814-  context-free
815-  \(L\subseteq\mathcal R_U\) has unbounded
816-  \(\omega(\val_U(w))\). More precisely, \(L\) contains a
817-  coprime-quotient chain \(N_{i+1}=N_iQ_i\) with
818-  \(Q_i>1\) and \(Q_i\equiv1\pmod {N_i}\). Thus the bounded-\(\omega\),
819:  bounded-\(\Omega\), and finite-prime-support languages of a unit
820-  system are MCF-immune whenever they are infinite. Without the unit
821:  hypothesis, every bounded-\(\Omega\) language is still MCF-immune.
822-\end{theorem}
823-
824-\begin{proof}
825-  The MCF-immunity assertions follow from
826:  \Cref{thm:nonunit-mcfl-escape-dichotomy}, including its
827:  bounded-\(\Omega\) conclusion. In a unit system \(S\) is empty, so
828-  that theorem gives unbounded \(\omega\). Taking
829-  \(M_i=r_i=1\) in
830-  \Cref{thm:unit-mcfl-deep-congruence-chain} gives the stated chain.
831-  Regular languages are context-free and context-free languages are
832-  MCFLs. Finally, \textup{(U2)} and Euclid's theorem make
833-  \(\mathcal P_U\) infinite.
834-\end{proof}

836-\begin{corollary}[Linear Pisot \(U\)-systems]
837-  \label{cor:linear-pisot-prime-cf-immunity}
838-  Let \(U=(U_n)_{n\ge0}\) be a linear Pisot \(U\)-system in the
839-  following precise sense: \(U_0=1\), the \(U_n\) are strictly increasing
840-  integers with bounded quotients, \(\mathcal R_U\) is the LSD-first
841-  reversal of the usual greedy representation language, and \(U\)
842-  eventually satisfies an integral recurrence whose characteristic
843-  polynomial is the minimal polynomial of a Pisot number. Then its prime
844-  representation language is MCF-immune, hence CF-immune, REG-immune and
845-  nonrecognizable. The same statements hold in the usual MSD-first
846-  convention.
847-
848-  If the dominant Pisot number is a unit and the chosen recurrence has
849-  trailing coefficient \(a_0=\pm1\), then the full coprime-quotient and
850:  bounded-prime-support MCF-immunity conclusions of
851-  \Cref{thm:recurrent-numeration-prime-cf-immunity} hold.
852-\end{corollary}
853-
854-\begin{proof}
855-  Greedy expansion gives a unique representation of every positive
856-  integer, and its length-\(m\) words represent values between successive
857-  place-value thresholds; thus \textup{(U1)--(U3)} hold. The defining
858-  Pisot recurrence gives \textup{(U4)}. Apply
859-  \Cref{thm:recurrent-numeration-prime-cf-immunity}. Frougny's finite
860-  normalization theorem supplies a finite transducer for normalization
861-  in this Pisot setting, and the associated canonical syntax and
862-  Bertrand/substitution descriptions are standard
863-  \cite{Frougny1992,BruyereHansel1997,Fabre1995,FrougnySolomyak1992}.
864-  Those finite-state results identify this corollary with the usual
865-  recognizability convention; the immunity proof itself uses only
866-  \textup{(U1)--(U4)}. Finally, multiple context-free, context-free, and
867-  regular languages are closed under reversal, so changing between the LSD-first proof
868-  convention and the usual MSD-first convention preserves every
869-  conclusion.
870-\end{proof}

872-\begin{example}[Unit and nonunit Pisot systems]
873-  \label{ex:pisot-unit-nonunit}
874-  The Fibonacci recurrence has characteristic polynomial
875-  \(X^2-X-1\), the Pell recurrence has \(X^2-2X-1\), and the
876-  Tribonacci recurrence has \(X^3-X^2-X-1\). Their trailing recurrence
877-  coefficient is \(a_0=1\), so the iterated conclusion applies. In
878:  ordinary base \(b\), \(U_n=b^n\) and \(a_0=b\); prime MCF-immunity
879-  follows, recovering the classical conclusion, but the unit iteration
880-  is not being asserted. A genuinely nonintegral, nonunit Pisot example
881-  is the dominant root \(1+\sqrt3\) of \(X^2-2X-2\): the recurrence
882-  \(U_{n+2}=2U_{n+1}+2U_n\) has \(a_0=2\), and the action is singular
883-  modulo \(2\).
884-\end{example}
885-
886-\begin{remark}[Exact open interfaces]
887-  \label{rem:pisot-open-interfaces}
888-  The terminology for Pisot numeration systems is not uniform.
889-  \Cref{cor:linear-pisot-prime-cf-immunity} covers the standard
890-  positional linear \(U\)-systems just specified, including integer
891-  bases, Zeckendorf/Fibonacci, Pell, and higher-order Pisot recurrences.
892-  It does not assert the theorem for arbitrary real-base
893-  \(\beta\)-shift representations, non-positional abstract numeration
894-  systems, redundant noninjective digit systems, or systems lacking an
895-  eventual integral recurrence and strict length ordering. Extending
896-  the argument to any of those classes requires a stationary finite
897-  block action that is invertible modulo represented primes.
898-
899-  For a fixed nonunit recurrence witness, the ambient action can be
900-  singular modulo primes dividing \(a_0\), so the unrestricted unit-system
901-  divisibility tree need not follow. The witness-relative surviving
902:  statement is \Cref{thm:nonunit-mcfl-escape-dichotomy}: every infinite
903:  MCFL must acquire unbounded prime support outside that finite set or
904-  unbounded valuation at one of its primes. The invariant restricted
905-  action and the failure of arbitrary recurrence witnesses to classify
906-  escape behavior are distinguished in
907-  \Cref{prop:recurrence-witness-separation}.
908-  The ordinary-base example preceding
909-  \Cref{thm:unit-mcfl-deep-congruence-chain} shows that the valuation
910-  alternative cannot be removed.
911-\end{remark}

         ON SUMS OF S-UNITS AND LINEAR RECURRENCES

                                     Jan-Hendrik Evertse

                                 §1. Introduction

In 1961 Chowla [1] proved that in any algebraic number field K there are
only finitely many pairs of units (1' E2 such that El - E2 = 1. Schlickewei
[15] and Dubois and Rhin [2] proved independently of each other that
the equation XI + X2 + ... + xn 0 = has only finitely many solutions in
rational integers XII X2, xn ..., which are pairwise coprime and each
composed of fixed primes. Recently, Shorey [20] showed that if {uk}~k=0
is a simple linear non-degenerate binary recurrence sequence of rational
integers, then the greatest prime factor of ur/us tends to infinity if
r ~ ~, r &#x3E; s, us ~ 0. It is our intention to generalize these results by a
uniform approach based on Schlickewei's p-adic version of the method of
Thue-Siegel-Roth-Schmidt. Part of our results has been obtained inde-
pendently by van der Poorten and Schlickewei [14].

   Throughout this paper, K will denote an algebraic number field of
degree D with ring of integers OK. By a prime on K we mean an
equivalence class of non-trivial valuations on K. We distinguish between
infinite primes which contain archimedean valuations and finite primes

which contain non-archimedean valuations. We denote the set of all

infinite primes on K by S~. There is a well-known correspondence
between finite primes and prime ideals. The letter p is used for primes on
Q, the letter v for primes on K. The infinite prime on Q is denoted by po

and 1.lpo is the ordinary absolute value. If q is a prime number in 0, the
corresponding finite prime is also denoted by q and 1.1|q denotes the q-adic

valuation defined in the usual way. The completions of 0, K at the

primes p, v respectively, are denoted by Qp, Kv respectively. Thus
Qp0 = R. For every prime v on K lying above a prime p on 0 we choose a

The Evertse source has now been checked at the primary-paper level, not merely by metadata. Its Theorem 3 is exactly the relevant input for nondegenerate recurrences with at least two characteristic roots; however, the manuscript’s proof compresses several necessary reductions into assertions (“each subsequence is nondegenerate,” rationality of the sole root, and the passage from rational-prime support to prime-ideal support). I am going to expand those steps explicitly so the lemma can withstand a referee reading the cited theorem literally.

# Literature and Novelty Check

Checked on 2026-08-02.  The arXiv searches below used the public Atom API
endpoint `https://export.arxiv.org/api/query`; DOI metadata was checked against
the Crossref REST API.  The purpose of the search was to delimit the theorem
claims, not to infer novelty from a null keyword search.

## arXiv API queries

The following literal `search_query` values were sent to the API (20 results
maximum per query):

- `all:"context-free" AND all:prime AND all:language`: four returned records,
  none on prime numeration languages.  The only mathematically related record
  was Borchert--Rampersad, *Inverse Star, Borders, and Palstars*,
  arXiv:1008.2440; it does not concern prime recognizability.
- `all:Pisot AND all:numeration AND all:automata`: eight returned records,
  including Carton--Couvreur--Delacourt--Ollinger,
  *Linear Recurrence Sequence Automata and the Addition of Abstract Numeration
  Systems*, arXiv:2406.09868 (conference DOI
  10.1007/978-3-031-97548-6_7); Charlier--Cisternino--Stipulanti,
  *Robustness of Pisot-regular sequences*, arXiv:2006.11126,
  DOI 10.1016/j.aam.2020.102151; Massuir--Peltomaki--Rigo,
  *Automatic sequences based on Parry or Bertrand numeration systems*,
  arXiv:1810.11081, DOI 10.1016/j.aam.2019.03.003; and
  Frougny--Steiner, *Minimal weight expansions in Pisot bases*,
  arXiv:0803.2874, DOI 10.1515/JMC.2008.017.  None of the returned records
  states prime-language REG- or CF-immunity.
- `all:"prime language" AND all:automata`: no returned records.
- `all:"abstract numeration systems" AND all:prime`: no returned records.
- `all:Ogden AND all:"interchange lemma"`: no returned records.  These are
  pre-arXiv classical papers and are cited by DOI below.
- Exact-title queries confirmed Dubbe, *The automaticity of the set of
  primes*, arXiv:2409.04314, DOI 10.1016/j.tcs.2025.115480, and Yuen,
  *Kleene Star of the Primes is not Regular in Any Base*, arXiv:2203.16088.

The arXiv API search is negative evidence only.  In particular, the older
JACM papers settle a stronger fixed-base question than their titles alone
suggest, so the paper does not advertise fixed-base CF-immunity as new.

## Exact classical citations

- William Ogden, "A helpful result for proving inherent ambiguity,"
  *Mathematical Systems Theory* 2 (1968), 191--194,
  DOI 10.1007/BF01694004.  This is the marked-position pumping lemma now
  called Ogden's lemma.
- William Ogden, Rockford J. Ross, and Karl Winklmann, "An 'Interchange
  Lemma' for Context-Free Languages," *SIAM Journal on Computing* 14 (1985),
  410--415, DOI 10.1137/0214031.  The present proof does not claim or reproduce
  their interchange lemma; ordinary context-free pumping suffices after a
  fixed-prefix quotient, while Ogden's lemma gives an alternative way to
  localize pumping beyond an eventual-recurrence transient.
- J. Hartmanis and H. Shank, "On the Recognition of Primes by Automata,"
  *Journal of the ACM* 15 (1968), 382--389,
  DOI 10.1145/321466.321470.
- M. P. Schutzenberger, "A Remark on Acceptable Sets of Numbers,"
  *Journal of the ACM* 15 (1968), 300--303,
  DOI 10.1145/321450.321461.  Contemporary citation records describe the
  Hartmanis--Shank and Schutzenberger conclusion as: no infinite set of
  base-`b` primes is recognized by a finite automaton or a pushdown automaton.
  Thus fixed-base prime CF-immunity is prior art.
- M. Minsky and S. Papert, "Unrecognizable Sets of Numbers,"
  *Journal of the ACM* 13 (1966), 281--286,
  DOI 10.1145/321328.321337.
- D. P. Allen, Jr., "On a characterization of the nonregular set of primes,"
  *Journal of Computer and System Sciences* 2 (1968), 464--467,
  DOI 10.1016/S0022-0000(68)80038-8.

## Pisot and numeration references

- Christiane Frougny, "Representations of numbers and finite automata,"
  *Mathematical Systems Theory* 25 (1992), 37--60,
  DOI 10.1007/BF01368783.  This is the normalization/finite-transducer source
  used for linear numeration systems whose characteristic polynomial has the
  Pisot property.
- Veronique Bruyere and Georges Hansel, "Bertrand numeration systems and
  recognizability," *Theoretical Computer Science* 181 (1997), 17--43,
  DOI 10.1016/S0304-3975(96)00260-5.
- Christiane Frougny and Boris Solomyak, "Finite beta-expansions,"
  *Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems* 12 (1992), 713--723,
  DOI 10.1017/S0143385700007057.
- Stephane Fabre, "Substitutions et beta-systemes de numeration,"
  *Theoretical Computer Science* 137 (1995), 219--236,
  DOI 10.1016/0304-3975(95)91132-A.
- P. B. A. Lecomte and M. Rigo, "Numeration Systems on a Regular Language,"
  *Theory of Computing Systems* 34 (2001), 27--44,
  DOI 10.1007/S002240010014.  This is cited to distinguish abstract
  numeration systems from the narrower linear Pisot `U`-systems proved here.

## Novelty boundary used in the manuscript

The following assertions are treated as new only relative to the literature
located above and are stated with their full hypotheses:

1. The two-pump block-action congruence modulo the square of the represented
   value and the resulting coprime-quotient chain for an arbitrary
   context-free sublanguage of canonical Zeckendorf representations.
2. CF-immunity of the Zeckendorf prime language, and the stronger unbounded
   distinct-prime-divisor consequences for context-free Zeckendorf
   sublanguages.
3. Prime REG- and CF-immunity for the explicitly defined class of positional
   linear Pisot `U`-systems: integer weights, finite digit alphabet, injective
   canonical representations ordered by length, and an eventual integral
   recurrence with nonzero trailing coefficient.  The proof uses only the
   recurrence block action; Frougny normalization supplies the standard
   finite-state canonical syntax/normalization interface for Pisot
   `U`-systems.

No claim is made for every object sometimes called a "Pisot numeration
system."  In particular, arbitrary real-base beta-shifts, non-positional
abstract numeration systems, systems without an eventual integral recurrence,
and non-injective redundant representations are explicit open interfaces.
The Pisot-unit hypothesis is needed for the unrestricted deep-quotient and
induced-tree conclusions and for unconditional bounded-omega immunity. For a
nonunit recurrence, primes dividing the trailing coefficient make the
companion action singular modulo some composite values. The local-adic
dichotomy nevertheless gives prime and bounded-Omega MCF-immunity; bounded
distinct-prime support can escape only through unbounded valuation at a prime
dividing the trailing coefficient.

<jats:p>A study of the problem of recognizing the set of primes by automata is presented. A simple algebraic condition is derived which shows that neither the set of primes nor any infinite subset of the set of primes can be accepted by a pushdown or finite automaton.</jats:p>
          <jats:p>In view of this result an interesting open problem is to determine the “weakest” automaton which can accept the set of primes. It is shown that the linearly bounded automaton can accept the set of primes, and it is conjectured that no automaton whose memory grows less rapidly can recognize the set of primes. One of the results shows that if this conjecture is true, it cannot be proved by the use of arguments about the distribution of primes, as described by the Prime Number Theorem. Some relations are established between two classical conjectures in number theory and the minimal rate of memory growth of automata which can recognize the set of primes.</jats:p>

                        "abstract":  "A study of the problem of recognizing the set of primes by automata is presented. A simple algebraic condition is derived which shows that neither the set of primes nor any infinite subset of primes can be accepted by a pushdown or finite automaton. In view of this result an interesting open problem is to determine the \"weakest\" automaton which can accept the set of primes. It is shown that the linearly bounded automaton can accept the set of primes, and it is conjectured that no automaton whose memory grows less rapidly can recognize the set of primes. One of the results shows that if this conjecture is true, it cannot be proved by the use of arguments about the distribution of primes, as described by the Prime Number Theorem. Some relations are established between two classical conjectures in number theory and the minimal rate of memory growth of automata which can recognize the set of primes",

                        "abstract":  "Oral cavity and oropharyngeal cancers are frequently described as part of a group of oral cancers or head and neck cancer. Treatment of oral cavity cancer is generally surgery followed by radiotherapy, whereas oropharyngeal cancers, which are more likely to be advanced at the time of diagnosis, are managed with radiotherapy or chemoradiation. Surgery for oral cancers can be disfiguring and both surgery and radiotherapy have significant functional side effects, notably impaired ability to eat, drink and talk. The development of new chemotherapy agents, new combinations of agents and changes in the relative timing of surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy treatments may potentially bring about increases in both survival and quality of life for this group of patients",

                        "abstract":  "Plan BThis was a descriptive study conducted in conjunction with the Department of Rehabilitation and Counseling. This study investigated the knowledge base of the rehabilitation professionals who provide job placement services to individuals with disabilities under Title I of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. It was also to investigate how they have implemented Title I while performing job placement activities. The results of this study were used to determine additional training needs of rehabilitation professionals as it relates to providing job placement services. The results were also used to determine how they have implemented Title I while assisting individuals with disabilities locate employment. The sample included 80 public sector and private non-profit sector rehabilitation professionals in Wisconsin. The participants were mailed a survey, asked to complete it, and return the survey by August 26, 2000. The knowledge base was determined by asking the Wisconsin Rehabilitation Association job placement division to report their knowledge by responding to statements generated from Title I in a true or false manner. They were asked to provide information about themselves in a confidential manner. Last they were asked to self-report, on a likert scale, how they have applied Title I of the ADA while performing job placement activities",

\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}

Finite-state symbolic models impose rigid constraints on counting
functions. In a deterministic automaton, the number of accepted words
of length \(m\) is governed by powers of a finite matrix. In a sofic
shift, the number of admissible words of a given length is likewise
controlled by a finite-state presentation. These mechanisms force
periodic density laws or exponential-polynomial growth, and that is
often enough to rule out arithmetic languages whose size is governed by
the prime number theorem.

This paper isolates a quantitative finite-budget obstruction. The first
part makes the fixed-base obstruction effective: from the DFA transition
matrix and explicit prime-counting bounds one computes the residue
alternatives, thresholds, and constants in the base-\(b\) prime-slice
comparison. The second part removes the strongly connected restriction
from the relative-density comparison. For an arbitrary trim
deterministic presentation with Perron root \(\lambda>1\), possibly
with several maximal strongly connected components and transient paths
between them, the Perron-scale residue classes have residue-wise
expansions with polynomial factors, while the remaining classes are
sub-Perron. Comparing the active polynomial exponents gives a
finite-budget obstruction for target families of size
\(\asymp\lambda^m/m\) on those active classes. The Zeckendorf
prime-slice results are then the strongly connected specialization of
this mechanism.

The language-theoretic part is independent of the prime number theorem.
After the Zeckendorf context-free argument, it combines the weak pumping
lemma for multiple context-free languages with the eventual affine
recurrence action. Every infinite MCFL then contains one increasing
orbit that returns simultaneously modulo every integer coprime to the
trailing recurrence coefficient. This yields a copy of \(\mathbb Q\) in
the associated deleted-congruence topology, a Cantor closure in the
completion, and an exact Cantor--Bendixson obstruction. Prime and
bounded-\(\Omega\) representation languages are MCF-immune even in the
nonunit case. In a unit recurrence witness, arbitrary-depth quotient
congruences produce an induced countably branching divisibility tree.
The trailing coefficient of a nonminimal witness is not a
numeration-system invariant: \Cref{prop:recurrence-witness-separation} exhibits
ordinary base \(p\) and an inflated Zeckendorf witness with the same
selected bad-prime set but opposite escape behavior.
Passing instead to the intrinsic minimal tail recurrence yields an exact
inverse statement: bounded prime support away from its constant term
occurs on an infinite MCFL precisely when the canonical language
contains a synchronized ray whose values are an integer geometric
progression. An explicit linear MCFG generates every such ray. When the
canonical syntax is supplied by a DFA, positive instances are
semidecidable; no general decision procedure is asserted.

For explicit Zeckendorf constants we use the canonical trim strongly
connected presentation, but the abstract finite-budget comparison in
\suppref{Theorem~1.14} applies to arbitrary trim
deterministic presentations. Numeration automata with multiple strongly
connected components do occur
\cite{CharlierRampersadRigoWaxweiler2010}; their polynomial factors are
accounted for in that theorem rather than excluded from the framework.

Throughout, \(f(m)\asymp g(m)\) means that \(c_1g(m)\le f(m)\le c_2g(m)\)
for some positive constants \(c_1,c_2\) and all sufficiently large
\(m\). We use the standard prime-counting convention
\(\pi(x)=\#\{p\le x:p\text{ prime}\}\). Thus an integer half-open
interval \([X,Y)\) contains exactly \(\pi(Y-1)-\pi(X-1)\) primes; in
asymptotic estimates below this may equivalently be written
\(\pi(Y)-\pi(X)+O(1)\). We write \(F_0=0\), \(F_1=1\) for the Fibonacci numbers,
\(\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2\), and for a Zeckendorf word
\(w=x_1\cdots x_m\) we set
\[
  \val(w):=\sum_{k=1}^m x_kF_{k+1}.
\]
For \(n\ge2\), \(\omega(n)\) denotes the number of distinct rational
prime divisors of \(n\), while \(\Omega(n)\) denotes the total number
of prime factors of \(n\), counted with multiplicity. We put
\(\omega(1)=\Omega(1)=0\), so \(\omega(n)\le\Omega(n)\) for all
\(n\ge1\).
\section{Further remarks}\label{sec:conclusion}

This paper proves a finite-budget obstruction for fixed finite-state
models facing prime-scale slices. The effective fixed-DFA theorem makes
the base-\(b\) obstruction computable from the transition matrix: the
residue alternatives, thresholds, and constants come from finite
Markov-chain linear algebra plus explicit prime-counting bounds. The
multicomponent presentation theorem keeps the residue-wise polynomial
factors on \(\lambda\)-active classes of arbitrary trim deterministic
presentations and compares those exponents against targets of size
\(\asymp\lambda^m/m\).

Together these results show that fixed-DFA approximation of prime
slices fails quantitatively: recall and precision cannot stay
simultaneously bounded below, and the symmetric difference from the
prime slice is always at least \(c_{\mathcal A,b}b^m/m\) in the ordinary
base-\(b\) setting and at least
\(c_{\mathcal A,\varphi}\varphi^m/m\) in the Zeckendorf setting. The
  Zeckendorf section also proves a sharper PNT-free language-theoretic
  obstruction. The unimodular action modulo \(N_i^2\) works for the two
  simultaneous pumps supplied by Ogden's lemma and gives the stated
  context-free coprime-quotient chain.

The same calculation depends only on a stationary affine companion
action. Under unique canonical representation, strict length ordering,
and an eventual integral recurrence with nonzero trailing coefficient,
the weak MCFL pumping lemma supplies one increasing orbit that is
periodic modulo every integer coprime to the trailing coefficient. Its
deleted-congruence subspace is a copy of \(\mathbb Q\), and its closure
in the corresponding profinite completion is a Cantor set. The exact
Cantor--Bendixson rank of bounded local prime-factor layers gives the
recurrence-witness-relative nonunit dichotomy: every infinite MCFL has
unbounded prime support away from the trailing coefficient or unbounded
valuation at one of its prime divisors. Thus prime and bounded-\(\Omega\) languages are
MCF-immune for all systems in the recurrent interface.

The selected trailing coefficient need not be intrinsic. In particular,
inflating the Fibonacci recurrence by \(X-p\) produces the
same selected bad-prime set as base \(p\) without producing its escape
language.

For the intrinsic minimal tail recurrence, the residual escape question
has an exact structural answer. An infinite MCFL with bounded prime
support away from the minimal constant term exists if and only if the
canonical language contains a synchronized pumping ray whose numerical
values are \(cb^t\) with integers \(c\ge1\) and \(b\ge2\). Such a ray has
an explicit finite-fan-out linear MCFG. With a DFA for the canonical
syntax, candidate rays can be enumerated and checked by finite-monoid
periodicity and exact recurrence identities, giving positive
semidecidability. Termination on negative instances, and hence general
decidability, remains open.

In a unit recurrence, the same fixed orbit realizes quotient
congruences of arbitrary prescribed depth. A recursive use of these
congruences embeds the full countably branching tree as an induced
divisibility suborder, with pairwise coprime edge quotients whose least
prime factors exceed arbitrary edge-wise thresholds. Standard linear
Pisot \(U\)-systems satisfy the recurrent interface; Frougny
normalization supplies their finite-state canonical syntax. In the
nonunit case, ordinary base-\(b\) powers show that the valuation escape
alternative is necessary. The final analytic appendix is only
contextual comparison.

Several natural questions remain outside the scope of this paper. The
density and finite-budget results use determinism essentially;
nondeterministic, weighted, or
bounded-ambiguity variants would require new hypotheses because
cancellation or ambiguity can change the counting problem. Broader
arithmetic targets other than primes are likewise future-work
directions rather than theorem claims here. Arbitrary real-base
\(\beta\)-shifts, redundant representations, and non-positional
abstract numeration systems also remain outside the theorem unless they
can be equipped with the stationary invertible block action isolated in
\Cref{rem:pisot-open-interfaces}.

The prior-art audit confirms that the fixed-base CF-immunity mechanism is classical and already cited honestly. The requested MCFL decision target is an immediate constant-NO corollary of the manuscript's stronger MCF-immunity theorem, so it cannot supply the requested tier upgrade. +## Refreshed prior-art and decision-target audit (2026-08-08)
+
+The two referee-critical classical records were rechecked against their
+publisher metadata and indexed abstracts, rather than inferred from their
+titles. Crossref gives DOI 10.1145/321466.321470 for Hartmanis--Shank and DOI
+10.1145/321450.321461 for Schutzenberger. The Hartmanis--Shank abstract states
+that neither the primes nor any infinite subset of the primes, in fixed-base
+notation, is accepted by a pushdown or finite automaton. The Schutzenberger
+abstract states that the two negative results on acceptable sets are extended
+to arbitrary context-free languages. CORE's Cornell record reproduces the
+Hartmanis--Shank abstract; Semantic Scholar and Unpaywall confirm the records
+and publisher copies. The manuscript already cites both papers where it calls
+fixed-base prime CF-immunity classical and explicitly says that their proofs
+are not reproduced as new.
+
+The reference lists supplied by Crossref were also inspected. They lead to
+the already cited Minsky--Papert paper on unrecognizable sets, the classical
+context-free-language sources, and the contemporary finite-automata work.
+No item in those lists concerns Zeckendorf or Pisot numeration, MCFLs, a
+recurrence block action, or the geometric-ray criterion.
+
+A live arXiv API query for `all:"multiple context-free" AND all:prime`
+returned zero records. Google Scholar searches for `"primes" "multiple
+context-free" language`, `"Pisot numeration" prime language automata`, and
+`"S-unit" "linear recurrence" geometric progression` returned the standard
+MCFG pumping literature, general numeration references, and recurrence/S-unit
+sources, but no prime-language result in Pisot numeration. Crossref searches
+confirmed the two 1968 JACM papers and their citation trails. A zbMATH API
+keyword search for `multiple context-free prime numeration` returned no
+record. OpenAlex exhausted its anonymous daily query budget during the audit,
+and the first Semantic Scholar search was rate-limited; these failures are
+recorded as failures, not as negative results.
+
+The proposed decision target does not define a new problem for the class
+proved in the manuscript. Theorem~3.17 proves that the prime representation
+language of every system satisfying (U1)--(U4) is MCF-immune, and Euclid's
+theorem plus canonical representation makes that language infinite.
+Consequently it is never an MCFL. For effectively presented regular canonical
+linear Pisot U-systems, the requested terminating algorithm is therefore the
+constant algorithm returning `NO`; this is an immediate corollary, not a
+tier-raising decision theorem.
+
+The genuinely nontrivial nearby decision problem is whether the bounded-
+outside-support condition in Theorem~3.14 holds, equivalently whether a
+geometric synchronized scheme exists. Corollary~3.15 gives only positive
+semidecidability. A full decision procedure would require an effective finite
+bound on the number and lengths of synchronized pumped blocks, or an
+equivalent negative certificate for the absence of exact geometric identities
+among recurrence sequences generated by finite transition and affine-matrix
+semigroups. No such bound follows from the cited pumping or recurrence
+theorems; general zero/equality questions for linear recurrences already meet
+Skolem-type barriers. The present tools therefore do not justify promoting
+that semidecision procedure to a decision theorem.

635-\begin{theorem}[Geometric-ray characterization]
636-  \label{thm:bounded-outside-support-geometric-ray}
637-  For a canonical eventually recurrent numeration system satisfying
638-  \textup{(U1)--(U4)}, the following are equivalent.
639-  \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
640-    \item There are a finite \(k\) and an infinite \(k\)-MCFL
641-    \(L\subseteq\mathcal R_U\) such that
642-    \[
643-      \sup_{w\in L}\omega_{S_{\mathrm r}^c}(\val_U(w))<\infty.
644-    \]
645-    \item The system admits a geometric synchronized scheme in the
646-    sense of \Cref{def:geometric-synchronized-scheme}.
647-    \item The language \(\mathcal R_U\) contains an infinite linear MCFL
648-    \(L_0=\{W(t):t\ge0\}\) of finite fan-out for which there are
649-    \(c\ge1,b\ge2\) satisfying
650-    \[
651-      \val_U(W(t))=cb^t\qquad(t\ge0).
652-    \]
653-  \end{enumerate}
654-\end{theorem}
655-
656-\begin{proof}
657-  Suppose first that \textup{(i)} holds. Use the minimal tail recurrence
658-  as the witness in
659-  \Cref{thm:mcfl-synchronized-congruence-orbit}, and write its resulting
660-  ray and strictly increasing value sequence as \(W(t)\) and \(N(t)\).
661-  Let
662-  \[
663-    K_0=\max_{t\ge0}\omega_{S_{\mathrm r}^c}(N(t)),
664-  \]
665-  and choose \(t_0\) attaining the maximum. Let \(T\) be the set of
666-  primes outside \(S_{\mathrm r}\) that divide \(N(t_0)\), and put
667-  \(q=\prod_{\ell\in T}\ell\). If \(T\ne\varnothing\), take the return
668-  time \(H=H(q)\) from
669-  \Cref{thm:mcfl-synchronized-congruence-orbit}; if \(T=\varnothing\),
670-  put \(H=1\). Every prime in \(T\) divides every \(N(t_0+nH)\). A prime
671-  divisor outside \(S_{\mathrm r}\cup T\) would therefore give at least
672-  \(K_0+1\) distinct prime divisors outside \(S_{\mathrm r}\), contrary
673-  to the definition of \(K_0\). Thus all terms of
674-  \[
675-    Y(n)=N(t_0+nH)
676-  \]
677-  are supported on the fixed finite set \(S_{\mathrm r}\cup T\).
678-
679-  The entries of every matrix power \(M^n\) satisfy a linear recurrence
680-  by Cayley--Hamilton. The expression for \(N(t)\) is a finite sum of
681-  finite products of such entries, and linear recurrence sequences are
682-  closed under sums and termwise products. Hence \(Y\) is a strictly
683-  increasing positive integer recurrence. By
684:  \Cref{lem:s-unit-increasing-recurrence-rigidity}, there are
685-  \(r\ge0,h\ge1,c\ge1,b\ge2\) such that
686-  \(N(t_\ast+h_\ast n)=cb^n\), where
687-  \(t_\ast=t_0+Hr\) and \(h_\ast=Hh\).
688-
689-  In the synchronized factorization, replace
690-  \[
691-    u_j\ \text{by}\ u_jv_j^{t_\ast},\qquad
692-    v_j\ \text{by}\ v_j^{h_\ast},\qquad
693-    w_j\ \text{by}\ w_js_j^{t_\ast},\qquad
694-    s_j\ \text{by}\ s_j^{h_\ast}.
695-  \]
696-  This absorbs the fixed powers and parametrizes exactly the subray
697-  \(W(t_\ast+h_\ast n)\). Its total pumped length remains positive, so
698-  it is a geometric synchronized scheme. This proves
699-  \textup{(i)}\(\Rightarrow\)\textup{(ii)}.
700-
701-  The implication \textup{(ii)}\(\Rightarrow\)\textup{(iii)} is
702-  \Cref{lem:synchronized-ray-linear-mcfg}. Finally, under
703-  \textup{(iii)}, the language \(L_0\) is an infinite MCFL and
704-  \[
705-    \omega_{S_{\mathrm r}^c}(cb^t)\le\omega(cb)
706-    \qquad(t\ge0),
707-  \]
708-  proving \textup{(i)}.
709-\end{proof}

711-\begin{corollary}[Positive semidecidability]
712-  \label{cor:bounded-outside-support-semidecidable}
713-  Suppose the numeration system is given effectively by its finite
714-  digit alphabet, recurrence and initial data, and a DFA recognizing
715-  \(\mathcal R_U\), with the minimal tail recurrence and a valid
716-  threshold \(J_{\mathrm r}\) effectively computable from these data.
717-  Then the property in
718-  \Cref{thm:bounded-outside-support-geometric-ray}\textup{(i)} is
719-  recursively enumerable, equivalently it has a \(\Sigma^0_1\) upper
720-  bound.
721-\end{corollary}

723-\begin{proof}
724-  Enumerate \(k\ge1\), \(a\in A^{J_{\mathrm r}}\), and all finite tuples
725-  of words occurring in
726-  \Cref{def:geometric-synchronized-scheme}, rejecting tuples of zero
727-  total pumped length. For a fixed tuple, whether the DFA accepts
728-  \(W(t)\) for every \(t\ge0\) is decidable: the tuple of powers of the
729-  finitely many pumped-block transformations is eventually periodic in
730-  the finite transition monoid, and its preperiod and period are found
731-  by exhaustive iteration.
732-
733-  The affine matrices construct an exact linear recurrence for
734-  \[
735-    N(t)=\val_U(W(t)).
736-  \]

743-  length equal to an explicitly constructed recurrence order. Thus each
744-  candidate scheme is decidable, and the enumeration halts exactly on
745-  positive instances by

747-  decision procedure for negative instances is made.

+## Refreshed prior-art and decision-target audit (2026-08-08)
+
+The two referee-critical classical records were rechecked against their
+publisher metadata and indexed abstracts, rather than inferred from their
+titles. Crossref gives DOI 10.1145/321466.321470 for Hartmanis--Shank and DOI
+10.1145/321450.321461 for Schutzenberger. The Hartmanis--Shank abstract states
+that neither the primes nor any infinite subset of the primes, in fixed-base
+notation, is accepted by a pushdown or finite automaton. The Schutzenberger
+abstract states that the two negative results on acceptable sets are extended
+to arbitrary context-free languages. CORE's Cornell record reproduces the
+Hartmanis--Shank abstract; Semantic Scholar and Unpaywall confirm the records
+and publisher copies. The manuscript already cites both papers where it calls
+fixed-base prime CF-immunity classical and explicitly says that their proofs
+are not reproduced as new.
+
+The reference lists supplied by Crossref were also inspected. They lead to
+the already cited Minsky--Papert paper on unrecognizable sets, the classical
+context-free-language sources, and the contemporary finite-automata work.
+No item in those lists concerns Zeckendorf or Pisot numeration, MCFLs, a
+recurrence block action, or the geometric-ray criterion.
+
+A live arXiv API query for `all:"multiple context-free" AND all:prime`
+returned zero records. Google Scholar searches for `"primes" "multiple
+context-free" language`, `"Pisot numeration" prime language automata`, and
+`"S-unit" "linear recurrence" geometric progression` returned the standard
+MCFG pumping literature, general numeration references, and recurrence/S-unit
+sources, but no prime-language result in Pisot numeration. Crossref searches
+confirmed the two 1968 JACM papers and their citation trails. A zbMATH API
+keyword search for `multiple context-free prime numeration` returned no
+record. OpenAlex exhausted its anonymous daily query budget during the audit,
+and the first Semantic Scholar search was rate-limited; these failures are
+recorded as failures, not as negative results.
+
+The proposed decision target does not define a new problem for the class
+proved in the manuscript. Theorem~3.17 proves that the prime representation
+language of every system satisfying (U1)--(U4) is MCF-immune, and Euclid's
+theorem plus canonical representation makes that language infinite.
+Consequently it is never an MCFL. For effectively presented regular canonical
+linear Pisot U-systems, the requested terminating algorithm is therefore the
+constant algorithm returning `NO`; this is an immediate corollary, not a
+tier-raising decision theorem.
+
+The genuinely nontrivial nearby decision problem is whether the bounded-
+outside-support condition in Theorem~3.14 holds, equivalently whether a
+geometric synchronized scheme exists. Corollary~3.15 gives only positive
+semidecidability. A full decision procedure would require an effective finite
+bound on the number and lengths of synchronized pumped blocks, or an
+equivalent negative certificate for the absence of exact geometric identities
+among recurrence sequences generated by finite transition and affine-matrix
+semigroups. No such bound follows from the cited pumping or recurrence
+theorems; general zero/equality questions for linear recurrences already meet
+Skolem-type barriers. The present tools therefore do not justify promoting
+that semidecision procedure to a decision theorem.

+## Refreshed prior-art and decision-target audit (2026-08-08)
+
+The two referee-critical classical records were rechecked against their
+publisher metadata and indexed abstracts, rather than inferred from their
+titles. Crossref gives DOI 10.1145/321466.321470 for Hartmanis--Shank and DOI
+10.1145/321450.321461 for Schutzenberger. The Hartmanis--Shank abstract states
+that neither the primes nor any infinite subset of the primes, in fixed-base
+notation, is accepted by a pushdown or finite automaton. The Schutzenberger
+abstract states that the two negative results on acceptable sets are extended
+to arbitrary context-free languages. CORE's Cornell record reproduces the
+Hartmanis--Shank abstract; Semantic Scholar and Unpaywall confirm the records
+and publisher copies. The manuscript already cites both papers where it calls
+fixed-base prime CF-immunity classical and explicitly says that their proofs
+are not reproduced as new.
+
+The reference lists supplied by Crossref were also inspected. They lead to
+the already cited Minsky--Papert paper on unrecognizable sets, the classical
+context-free-language sources, and the contemporary finite-automata work.
+No item in those lists concerns Zeckendorf or Pisot numeration, MCFLs, a
+recurrence block action, or the geometric-ray criterion.
+
+A live arXiv API query for `all:"multiple context-free" AND all:prime`
+returned zero records. Google Scholar searches for `"primes" "multiple
+context-free" language`, `"Pisot numeration" prime language automata`, and
+`"S-unit" "linear recurrence" geometric progression` returned the standard
+MCFG pumping literature, general numeration references, and recurrence/S-unit
+sources, but no prime-language result in Pisot numeration. Crossref searches
+confirmed the two 1968 JACM papers and their citation trails. A zbMATH API
+keyword search for `multiple context-free prime numeration` returned no
+record. OpenAlex exhausted its anonymous daily query budget during the audit,
+and the first Semantic Scholar search was rate-limited; these failures are
+recorded as failures, not as negative results.
+
+The proposed decision target does not define a new problem for the class
+proved in the manuscript. Theorem~3.17 proves that the prime representation
+language of every system satisfying (U1)--(U4) is MCF-immune, and Euclid's
+theorem plus canonical representation makes that language infinite.
+Consequently it is never an MCFL. For effectively presented regular canonical
+linear Pisot U-systems, the requested terminating algorithm is therefore the
+constant algorithm returning `NO`; this is an immediate corollary, not a
+tier-raising decision theorem.
+
+The genuinely nontrivial nearby decision problem is whether the bounded-
+outside-support condition in Theorem~3.14 holds, equivalently whether a
+geometric synchronized scheme exists. Corollary~3.15 gives only positive
+semidecidability. A full decision procedure would require an effective finite
+bound on the number and lengths of synchronized pumped blocks, or an
+equivalent negative certificate for the absence of exact geometric identities
+among recurrence sequences generated by finite transition and affine-matrix
+semigroups. No such bound follows from the cited pumping or recurrence
+theorems; general zero/equality questions for linear recurrences already meet
+Skolem-type barriers. The present tools therefore do not justify promoting
+that semidecision procedure to a decision theorem.

import unittest

from artifacts import verify_pisot_pumping as verifier


class PisotPumpingVerifierTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_tail_action_starts_after_the_eventual_recurrence_transient(self):
        recurrence = (-10, 7)
        weights = (1, 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, 96, 192)
        prefix = (2,)

        for suffix_length in range(6):
            for suffix_number in range(1 << suffix_length):
                suffix = tuple(
                    (suffix_number >> index) & 1
                    for index in range(suffix_length)
                )
                transformed = verifier.tail_action_state(
                    recurrence, weights, prefix, suffix
                )
                full_word = prefix + suffix
                expected = (
                    sum(
                        digit * weight
                        for digit, weight in zip(full_word, weights)
                    ),
                    *weights[len(full_word) : len(full_word) + len(recurrence)],
                )
                self.assertEqual(transformed, expected)

    def test_explicit_linear_mcfg_ray_realizes_a_geometric_base_two_orbit(self):
        base_two = verifier.system_by_name("integer_base_2")
        values = []
        for exponent in range(13):
            word = verifier.linear_mcfg_ray_word(
                prefix=(),
                constants=((), (1,)),
                left_pumps=((0,),),
                middles=((),),
                right_pumps=((),),
                exponent=exponent,
            )
            self.assertEqual(word, (0,) * exponent + (1,))
            values.append(verifier.value(base_two, word))

        self.assertEqual(values, [2**exponent for exponent in range(13)])

    def test_affine_action_matches_direct_evaluation(self):
        for system in verifier.SYSTEMS:
            with self.subTest(system=system.name):
                verifier.check_affine_action(system, max_length=7)

    def test_two_block_return_gives_square_modulus_congruence(self):
        fib = verifier.system_by_name("fibonacci")
        word = (0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1)  # 23 in LSD-first Zeckendorf form
        witness = verifier.verify_pump_witness(
            fib,
            word,
            cuts=(2, 3, 4, 5),
            require_canonical=True,
        )
        self.assertEqual(witness.original_value, 23)
        self.assertGreater(witness.pump_exponent, 1)
        self.assertEqual(witness.pumped_value % (23 * 23), 23)
        self.assertGreater(witness.pumped_value, 23)
        self.assertEqual(witness.pumped_value // 23 % 23, 1)

    def test_nonunit_bad_prime_is_rejected(self):
        nonunit = verifier.system_by_name("quadratic_nonunit")
        with self.assertRaises(verifier.NonInvertibleAction):
            verifier.matrix_order(
                verifier.block_matrix(nonunit, (0,)), modulus=2
            )

    def test_counterexample_search_finds_required_hypothesis(self):
        witness = verifier.search_singular_counterexample()
        self.assertEqual(witness["system"], "quadratic_nonunit")
        self.assertEqual(witness["modulus"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(witness["trailing_coefficient"], 2)
        self.assertFalse(witness["invertible"])

        self.assertGreater(report["cases"], 100)
        self.assertEqual(report["failures"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(report["reachable_rank"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(report["reachable_determinant"], -1)

    def test_synchronized_multi_block_orbit_for_all_tested_parameters(self):
        fibonacci = verifier.system_by_name("fibonacci")
        word = (0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1)
        spans = ((2, 3), (4, 5))
        cases = verifier.check_synchronized_orbit(
            fibonacci,
            word,
            spans,
            moduli=range(2, 21),
            parameters=range(6),
        )
        self.assertEqual(cases, 19 * 6)

        nonunit = verifier.system_by_name("quadratic_nonunit")
        with self.assertRaises(verifier.NonInvertibleAction):
            verifier.check_synchronized_orbit(
                nonunit,
                (1, 0, 0, 1),
                ((1, 2), (2, 3)),
                moduli=(2,),
                parameters=(0,),
            )

    def test_local_layer_isolation_certificate(self):
        n = 2 * 3 * 5**2 * 7
        excluded_primes = (2, 3)
        valuation_bounds = {2: 2, 3: 1}
        modulus = verifier.local_layer_isolation_modulus(
            n, excluded_primes, valuation_bounds
        )
        self.assertEqual(verifier.omega_outside(n, excluded_primes), 2)
        self.assertEqual(verifier.gcd(modulus, 2 * 3), 1)

        congruent_layer_points = [
            m
            for m in range(1, 50_001)
            if verifier.in_local_prime_layer(
                m, 2, excluded_primes, valuation_bounds
            )
            and (m - n) % modulus == 0
        ]
        self.assertEqual(congruent_layer_points, [n])

    def test_deep_chain_has_prescribed_congruence_depth(self):
        specifications = ((6, 1), (30, 2), (210, 1))
        chain = verifier.construct_deep_congruence_chain(2, specifications)
        for current, following, (modulus_factor, depth) in zip(
            chain, chain[1:], specifications
        ):
            quotient = following // current
            self.assertGreater(quotient, 1)
            self.assertEqual(following % current, 0)
            self.assertEqual(
                quotient % (modulus_factor * current**depth), 1
            )

    def test_finite_divisibility_tree_is_induced_and_has_coprime_edges(self):
        nodes = ((), (0,), (1,), (0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0))
        thresholds = {
            (0,): 3,
            (1,): 5,
            (0, 0): 7,
            (0, 1): 11,
            (1, 0): 13,
        }
        values, edge_quotients = verifier.construct_divisibility_tree(
            root=2, nodes=nodes, thresholds=thresholds
        )
        for left in nodes:
            for right in nodes:
                self.assertEqual(
                    values[right] % values[left] == 0,
                    right[: len(left)] == left,
                )
        quotients = list(edge_quotients.values())
        for index, left in enumerate(quotients):
            for right in quotients[index + 1 :]:
                self.assertEqual(verifier.gcd(left, right), 1)
        for edge, quotient in edge_quotients.items():
            for prime in range(2, thresholds[edge] + 1):
                if verifier.is_prime(prime):
                    self.assertNotEqual(quotient % prime, 0)
